item.title: Summer Box Office Reaches $4.6 Billion Recovery
item.description:
Summer Box Office Tops $4.6 Billion: Hollywood’s Post-Pandemic Victory

Industry Marks Significant Recovery Milestone

The entertainment industry has reached a pivotal moment in its recovery trajectory. With the summer box office season concluding at an impressive $4.6 billion, Hollywood is demonstrating remarkable resilience and consumer appetite for theatrical experiences. This substantial figure represents far more than just financial metrics—it symbolizes the industry’s successful navigation through unprecedented challenges and signals renewed confidence in cinema’s cultural relevance.

item.title: Cruise Confirms Days of Thunder Sequel
item.description:
Cruise Confirms Days of Thunder Sequel

Tom Cruise announced a Days of Thunder sequel with Anne Hathaway in a Saturday video from Daytona International Speedway, posing beside a lime-green NASCAR car tagged for summer 2028. The confirmation did not arrive as a rumor dressed up as news. It arrived as the star standing at the sport’s most famous oval, next to sheet metal already labeled for a summer still almost two years away, and naming a co-star whose presence immediately became the other half of the story.

item.title: Dolly’s Wish Mended Cyrus Rift
item.description:
Dolly’s Wish Mended Cyrus Rift

Dolly Parton died Tuesday, August 25, at 80, after a brief battle with cancer. The death of the “Jolene” singer closed a public life that had run for decades in country music and, according to a National Examiner source carried on Yahoo, closed a private role as well: godmother, guiding light, and the person Miley Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus now say they intend to honor by ending the family fighting that had torn them apart.

item.title: Cruise Green-Flags Thunder Sequel 2028
item.description:
Cruise Green-Flags Thunder Sequel 2028

Tom Cruise, 64, did not walk onto the Daytona stage the way a studio executive walks onto a panel. On Saturday he hopped a row of potted plants to get there, then told 40 Cup drivers the sentence the stock-car world has been waiting almost a generation to hear: he is bringing Cole Trickle back.

The gesture was pure Cruise — physical, slightly ridiculous, impossible to ignore — and it was also a piece of calendar work. Paramount has dated the Days of Thunder follow-up for June 2, 2028, nearly 40 years after Tony Scott’s 1990 NASCAR film. The announcement did not arrive as a sterile studio graphic. It arrived as a man of 64 climbing over landscaping in front of the people who actually drive Cup cars for a living.

item.title: Cruise Recruits Hathaway For Thunder Sequel
item.description:
Cruise Recruits Hathaway For Thunder Sequel

Hollywood has spent the better part of four decades treating Days of Thunder as a period piece that happened to mint a star marriage and a NASCAR aesthetic. On Saturday, Paramount treated it as a living franchise. The studio locked a sequel that pairs Tom Cruise with Anne Hathaway, plants a June 2, 2028 theatrical date on the calendar, and hands the keys back to Cole Trickle — the cocky stock-car driver Cruise first played in Tony Scott’s 1990 racing film. Plot details stay sealed. The image that announced the movie does not.

item.title: Tom Hardy Raps Shakespeare As Bane
item.description:
Tom Hardy Raps Shakespeare As Bane

Tom Hardy has spent fifteen years proving he can disappear into a voice. On Friday he disappeared into a name. Under the alias Frankie Pulitzer, the British actor dropped a 15-track rap album, a collaboration with the underground trio Czarface — 7L & Esoteric plus Wu-Tang’s Inspectah Deck — titled Czarface Meets Frankie Pulitzer. Features include Busta Rhymes, Method Man, and EL-P. The verses are stuffed with movie and comic Easter eggs. The moment that will travel is the one that sounds like a joke until you sit with it: on “Grim-Visaged War,” Hardy recites Shakespeare’s Richard III monologue in the muffled Bane voice from The Dark Knight Rises.

item.title: Written-Off Coyote Humiliates Warner At Box
item.description:
Written-Off Coyote Humiliates Warner At Box

Three years after Warner Bros. tried to disappear him for a tax write-off, Wile E. Coyote opened a movie. Coyote vs. Acme, the Looney Tunes hybrid the studio killed in 2023, arrived Friday via indie Ketchup Entertainment and is tracking about $14 million from 3,575 theaters. That is a record start for the distributor, more than four times its prior high of $3.1 million. It is also a public embarrassment for the conglomerate that decided a finished comedy was worth more as a deduction than as a release.
